summary: In a courtroom scene from Book 1, the narrator Mr Yallow faces a judge after prisoners held since the bridge blew up are brought to court. The judge considers holding him for trial as a flight risk, but the narrator explains he chose to face justice rather than run, after stealing and then returning a phone containing evidence about his friend Darryl Glover. The judge grants bail, adds a misdemeanor petty theft charge, and sets an additional $50,000 bail.
one_line: Mr Yallow appears before a tired judge, explains why he stayed to face justice after stealing a phone, and wins bail with an added theft charge.
key_facts: Mr Yallow is brought before a judge who calls him a flight risk and says he has more history than the other people in the courtroom.
The ACLU lawyer asked the judge for a few more hours while the prisoners' families were rounded up and brought to the courthouse.
Some of the prisoners had been locked up since the bridge blew, were taken for dead by their families, and were held without trial.
The judge rapped his gavel once and scrubbed at his eyes while looking tired.
Mr Yallow says he had the chance to run last week when someone offered to take him away and help build a new identity.
Mr Yallow stole a phone, escaped from the truck, and ran away instead of running from justice.
The phone contained evidence about Mr Yallow's friend, Darryl Glover, and Mr Yallow gave it to a journalist before hiding out in town.
Mr Yallow says he decided he could not run because his freedom was not worth anything while his friends were still locked up.
Mr Yallow admits he stole the phone and plans to give it back if he finds the young woman in question.
The judge says a video on the news that morning suggested Mr Yallow had a legitimate reason to evade the authorities.
The judge grants bail and asks the prosecutor to add a charge of Misdemeanor Petty Theft regarding the phone.
The judge sets an additional $50,000 bail for the petty theft charge.
The judge calls Mr Yallow a very well spoken and possibly very brave young man.
Mr Yallow's lawyer squeezes his hand after the gavel bangs again.
